coreIdea: Recognize the SHAPE of code first (GCD, power, binary conversion, rotation, transpose) before tracing. General-formula questions reward pattern-matching; specific-value questions reward direct tracing.
mustRememberFormulas: Recursive squaring (x*=x, n/=2): x^n in O(log n)
Recursive call BEFORE print, divide by 2: prints binary (MSB first)
Three reversals (0..k, k+1..n, 0..n): rotates array left by k+1

patternRecognitionTable.seeThis: recursive code, asked 'what function does this compute' (general)
specific input given, asked exact numeric output
iterative loop building a value, asked what it approximates for large n
array/matrix index manipulation, asked overall transformation

commonTrapsQuickList: Don't brute-force trace when a general formula is asked — recognize the shape first
Recursive-call-before-print = MSB first; after-print = LSB first
Matrix transpose loops need i<j guard, else double-swap can undo itself
For 'exact output' questions, direct tracing IS the fastest approach — don't over-search for shortcuts
highYieldPyqLessons: General-formula identification (15/38) is the single biggest sub-skill and the most time-saving once mastered — build a mental library of the ~6 recurring shapes (GCD, power, binary conversion, rotation, transpose, merge).
This topic is the 'capstone' of the DS+Algorithms track — it draws on Recursion, Pointers, and Programming-In-C all at once.
